title: Taniya Wins Silver in Beach Wrestling's Youth Olympic Debut at Dakar
excerpt: The Indian wrestler lost the women's 75kg final 1-2 to China's Zhao Min after four straight wins — becoming the first Indian to medal in the sport at a Youth Olympics.
body:
• India's Taniya won silver in the women's 75kg beach wrestling at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, losing 1-2 to China's Zhao Min in the final on Saturday, November 7.
  • She is the first Indian wrestler to win a Youth Olympics medal in beach wrestling, a sport making its debut at these Games.
  • Taniya reached the final unbeaten, with four straight wins including a 4-1 quarter-final victory and a 3-1 semi-final win over the USA's Matilda Ann Hruby.
  • Beach wrestling is contested on sand inside a seven-metre circle; Dakar 2026 runs from October 31 to November 13 and is the first IOC event held in Africa.

India's Taniya took the silver medal in the women's 75kg beach wrestling at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Saturday, losing a tight gold-medal bout 1-2 to China's Zhao Min at Saly Beach West in Senegal. The result makes her the first Indian wrestler to win a Youth Olympics medal in beach wrestling, in the very edition where the sport has been introduced to the Games.

A final that turned on one point

Taniya started the final the stronger of the two, taking an early 1-0 lead, according to reports from Dakar. Zhao drew level and then scored the decisive point to win by Victory by Points. The defeat was Taniya's first of the competition — she had won all four of her bouts before the final.

Her run through the draw underlined how close she came to gold. In the quarter-finals she beat Estonia's Merily Vaester 4-1, and in the semi-finals she defeated Matilda Ann Hruby of the United States 3-1 to guarantee India a medal. Hruby went on to take bronze.

A debut sport, a landmark medal

Beach wrestling is a fast-paced version of the sport contested on sand within a seven-metre circular area, and Dakar 2026 is its first appearance at a Youth Olympic Games. Medalling in a discipline's debut edition gives Taniya's silver a permanent place in the record books: whenever beach wrestling's Youth Olympic history is written, an Indian name is on its first podium.

Zhao arrived in the final with a strong pedigree of her own — she won the women's 69kg title at the 2025 Athens U17 World Championships — which makes the one-point margin of the final a fair measure of how competitive Taniya was against the field's standout wrestler.

India's wider day on the sand

Taniya's silver closed out India's beach wrestling campaign at Dakar. In the men's 80kg category, Deepanshu Khokhar did not progress to the medal rounds, losing his bouts to Morocco's Abdeljalil Benelyassar, Azerbaijan's Nihad Suleymanli and Algeria's Yasser Kraled Kebir, according to Revsportz.

Dakar 2026, the fourth edition of the Summer Youth Olympic Games, runs for 14 days from October 31 to November 13, 2026, and is the first International Olympic Committee event staged in Africa. For India's young wrestlers — most of whom train for the mat, not the sand — a silver medal in a debut discipline is a result the federation can build on as beach wrestling looks for a place in the senior calendar.
